text:
hayes: Tried working from the balcony today with a hammock. 10/10 views, 2/10 wifi. Posted a pic: https://files.slack.com/archives/random/FVAL1234/IMG_20260503.jpg

rachel: Love the vibe. Quick tip: turn off auto-join to 2.4Ghz and force 5Ghz if available. The balcony is usually cluttered on the lower band.

mike: If the router is inside, try a long USB ethernet adapter + short outdoor-rated ethernet run to a small travel router. Been my go-to for patios.

hayes: I tried the phone hotspot and it was fine for calls but streaming demos died. Any low-effort boosters?

zoe: Pocket travel router with external antenna helped me. Also point it toward the balcony window. I used a recycled phone as a bridge once.

infra-bot: Tip: "When working outdoors, prioritize audio settings over video. Lower video to 360p, disable HD, and enable background noise suppression for reliable calls." :robot_face:

rachel: Also try sitting near the window with a towel behind you to reduce wind noise. Hammock swinging + mic = odd echoes. :sweat_smile:

hayes: Good call. Pulled the hammock closer to the sliding door, forced 5Ghz, and moved the router to the sill. Demo survived. Will invest in a small travel AP for future sunny days. Thanks all! :sun_with_face:
